deck.title: Direct Connect & VPN
deck.analogy: Site-to-Site VPN is an armored car on public roads; Direct Connect is your own private toll road straight to AWS.

cards.front: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect: what is the analogy for each?

back.answer: VPN is an armored car on public roads (encrypted over the internet); Direct Connect is your own private toll road.
back.explanation: VPN is fast to arrange and cheap but shares the internet, so latency varies. DX is consistent and private but slow to build.
back.mnemonic: Armored car (VPN) vs private toll road (DX).

cards.front: What does an AWS Site-to-Site VPN use to protect traffic, and over what network?

back.answer: An encrypted IPsec tunnel over the public internet.
back.explanation: Latency varies because the internet is shared.

cards.front: What is the setup time and cost profile of AWS Site-to-Site VPN?

back.answer: Setup takes hours; cheap — a small hourly charge plus data transfer.

cards.front: What is the approximate throughput of a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel?

back.answer: About 1.25 Gbps per tunnel, with variable latency.

cards.front: Site-to-Site VPN: what is the Virtual Private Gateway (VGW)?

back.answer: The AWS-side VPN endpoint attached to your VPC.

cards.front: Site-to-Site VPN: what is the Customer Gateway (CGW)?

back.answer: Your side's representation of your on-prem router/firewall.

cards.front: What is AWS Client VPN and when do you use it?

back.answer: It connects individual laptops to a VPC — for remote employees, not for connecting a datacenter.

cards.front: What is AWS Direct Connect?

back.answer: Dedicated private fiber from your location to AWS that never touches the public internet.

cards.front: What bandwidths does Direct Connect offer, and how is its performance?

back.answer: 1, 10, or 100 Gbps with consistent bandwidth and low latency.

cards.front: How long does Direct Connect take to set up?

back.answer: Weeks to months, because someone has to physically run fiber.

cards.front: Is Direct Connect encrypted by default, and how do you add encryption?

back.answer: No. Run a Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec) over the Direct Connect link.
back.explanation: Private is not the same as encrypted.

cards.front: Direct Connect: where does a Private VIF go?
Direct Connect: where does a Public VIF go?

back.answer: To AWS public services (S3, DynamoDB endpoints).

cards.front: Direct Connect: where does a Transit VIF go?
What does a Direct Connect Gateway do?

back.answer: Lets one DX connection reach many VPCs across many regions.
back.explanation: No separate fiber per VPC is needed.

cards.front: Direct Connect: what is the classic cost-effective backup?

back.explanation: The classic exam pattern is DX + VPN failover.

cards.front: Direct Connect: how do you get maximum resiliency, and what is the tradeoff?

back.answer: Two DX connections, ideally at different locations; maximum cost.

cards.front: You need AWS connectivity this week but DX fiber is still being installed. What do you do?

back.answer: Start with Site-to-Site VPN, then cut over to Direct Connect when ready.

cards.front: When do you choose Site-to-Site VPN over Direct Connect?

back.answer: When you need it in hours, cheap, and encrypted.

cards.front: When do you choose Direct Connect, and what combo gives both reliability worlds?

back.answer: Consistent performance, large steady data, or no public internet; combine DX primary with VPN backup.

cards.front: Transferring 5 TB nightly to AWS; Site-to-Site VPN performance is inconsistent. Best fix?

back.explanation: Dedicated fiber gives consistent throughput for big regular transfers.

choices.why: For individual devices, not bulk site transfers.
Still over the variable public internet.
Needs a DX connection; doesn't fix performance.

cards.front: Company needs a cost-effective backup for an existing Direct Connect link. What is the answer?

choices.why: Goes to public services, not a backup.

cards.front: Data over Direct Connect must be encrypted in transit. What do you do?

back.answer: Run a Site-to-Site VPN over the DX connection.

choices.text: Nothing; DX is encrypted by default
choices.why: DX is not encrypted by default.
For individual devices, not site links.
Adds IPsec on the private link.

cards.front: Must connect on-premises to AWS within days. Which option?

back.explanation: DX takes weeks–months; VPN takes hours.

cards.front: Remote employees' laptops need secure access to the VPC. Which service?
One Direct Connect must reach VPCs in multiple regions. What do you use?

choices.why: One DX reaches many VPCs and regions.

cards.front: On-prem must reach AWS with no traffic on the public internet. Which option?

back.explanation: The only option that skips the internet entirely.

choices.why: Still travels over the public internet.
